title: Omega-6 fats for the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease
authors: Hooper L, Al-Khudairy L, Abdelhamid AS, Rees K, Brainard JS, Brown TJ, et al.
population: 19 randomised trials of higher versus lower omega-6 fat intake in adults with or without cardiovascular disease, at least 12 months
funder: Internal sources: University of East Anglia; Warwick Medical School, University of Warwick. External sources: the World Health Organization funded this update, commissioned to underpin WHO guidance on polyunsaturated fats; the original version was supported by a NIHR Cochrane Programme Grant; NIHR CLAHRC West Midlands; NIHR Cochrane Infrastructure funding to the Heart Group.
authorConflicts: WHO funding to the University of East Anglia paid the employment of several authors; no other conflicts declared.
result: Increasing omega-6 fat: all-cause mortality RR 1.00 (95% CI 0.88 to 1.12; 740 deaths, 4506 randomised, 10 trials, low quality), 167 per 1000 with lower and 167 per 1000 with higher omega-6 fat; myocardial infarction RR 0.88 (0.76 to 1.02; 609 events, 4606 participants, 7 trials, low quality), 53 people to increase omega-6 fat to prevent one infarction; total serum cholesterol -0.33 mmol/L (-0.50 to -0.16; 10 trials, high quality); LDL cholesterol -0.04 mmol/L (-0.21 to 0.14; 2 trials, low quality). All-cause mortality in trials without commercial funding RR 1.19 (0.84 to 1.69; 4 trials, 1208 participants). The Minnesota Coronary trial was excluded because most participants were not in the study continuously for at least one year.
